policy_title: Cut Cost of Net Zero for Consumers
stated: The Conservative Party will cut the cost of net zero for consumers by guaranteeing no new green levies or charges, ensuring annual policy costs on energy bills are lower than in 2023, and reforming the Climate Change Committee to consider cost to households and energy security.

source.quote: Cut the cost of net zero for consumers by taking a more pragmatic approach, guaranteeing no new green levies or charges while accelerating the rollout of renewables. ...Ensuring that green levies on household bills are lower. ...Reforming the Climate Change Committee, giving it an explicit mandate to consider cost to households and UK energy security in its future climate advice.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets energy bill costs for households by capping/cutting green levies, with a stated commitment to keep annual policy costs lower than 2023 levels — a non-negligible effect on disposable income and energy affordability.
Reforming the Climate Change Committee and constraining green levies affects the pace and ambition of UK net zero policy, with plausible non-negligible effect on emissions trajectory.

membership_note: Two clean signals: O2 (designed-for benefit — lower bills) and O6 (cross-outcome harm — weakened climate governance and reduced transition funding). O11 is not in scope as green levies act on energy bills not income/payroll; O12 is not materially affected as levies are off-balance-sheet consumer charges rather than fiscal expenditure.
